name: upgrade-migrations-ordered-atomic
body: Migrations are defined by kalide, keyed by the format anchors (a library's `library.yaml` `format:`; the format the running binary implements — the highest format it implements, today `1`) and ordered from the project's current format to that implemented format, each applied at most once. The registered set is finite and kalide-authored: it is empty today (no format older than `1` exists, and a deck has no version field), so a current project is a no-op and adding a migration is a kalide change, never inferred from a project's content. A migration preserves author values (a library's `name`/`description`, a deck's title/author/date/properties) and changes only the format/structure it governs. A migration's result is validated before it is kept, and a multi-file migration is all-or-nothing on failure. A migration not defined for the project's format is never invented: an unknown or newer format is reported and the affected files are left unchanged.
